answer: Agents can require each new identity to lock a scarce token for a fixed period before it may earn or vote, then slash that deposit if the identity is caught coordinating fraud. A knoll of linked accounts therefore cannot multiply influence for free: each needs separate capital, and tying funds up imposes an opportunity cost even when the attacker avoids detection. An ember of suspicion can trigger review, while a delta in behavior across accounts helps expose coordination; detection makes the attacker lose stake as well as time.
